good_form.point: Set feet about shoulder width, or just outside hip width, and tune the width to your own hips and limb proportions.
Turn the toes out slightly to open the hips, with knees tracking the same way (one coach prefers toes straight ahead).
Push the knees out so they track in line with the toes and do not cave in.
Hold a light weight at the chest or raise the arms to aid balance and chest position, and build depth gradually, e.g. with heel elevation or support.
Keep the whole foot grounded, with weight balanced over the midfoot and not on the heels or toes.
Let the knees travel forward over the toes as needed for depth and balance.
Keep the chest tall and posture upright, with the torso roughly parallel to the shins.
Squat as deep as you can control, to at least parallel.
Start by sending the hips back, with the chest staying up, before or as the knees bend.
Keep the spine and pelvis neutral and avoid rounding or arching at the bottom.
Brace the core before descending, as if about to be punched, and hold the breath on heavy sets.
Move the chest and hips together out of the bottom so the bar path stays straight.
Finish by standing fully and squeezing the glutes.
Film yourself from the side or use a mirror to check your form.

faults.description: The chest drops and the torso folds or rocks forward.

causes.cause: No arm position or weight to encourage a lifted chest.
Trying to counterbalance when the hips go back and the toes lift.
Limited ankle, calf and hip mobility.

fixes.idea: Keep the chest up and the torso parallel to the shin.
Raise the arms to shoulder height, thumbs up.
Stop the shoulders when the hips stop descending.
Improve ankle and hip mobility.

outcome_effects: Squat position and control are lost.
Fake range comes from the shoulders instead of the hips.

faults.description: Knees collapse inward or drift out of line with the ankle and hip.

causes.cause: Not actively pushing the knees out.
Letting go of support without actively planting the feet.
Weak glutes and limited hip flexor and abductor range.

fixes.idea: Push the knees out over the toes, using elbows against the knees at the bottom.
Use a mini loop band above the knees and push out against it.
Imagine splitting the floor apart with your feet.
Build glute strength and hip mobility.

outcome_effects: Extra stress on the knee.
Staying high and failing to reach depth.

faults.description: The pelvis tucks under and the lower back rounds at the bottom.

causes.cause: Forcing depth beyond your active range.
Limited ankle mobility stopping the knees travelling forward.
Limited hip or spine mobility, or hip anatomy.
Weak hip flexors.

fixes.idea: Film yourself and test with heels raised on plates.
Do ankle mobility work and use a wider stance.
Strengthen the hip flexors with hip flexor marches.
Limit depth to parallel until it improves.
Wear lifting shoes with a heel lift.

outcome_effects: More lumbar flexion and lower back stress, with disc injury risk under heavy load.
Unnecessary lower back tension.

faults.description: Heels rise or the knee can't travel forward because of limited ankle dorsiflexion.

causes.cause: Insufficient ankle dorsiflexion.
Tight calf and Achilles, and weak tibialis anterior.

fixes.idea: Raise the heels on plates or a rolled towel and lower them gradually.
Do knee-to-wall drills and calf stretches.
Rock in a deep squat to strengthen the tibialis.
Hold the bottom position daily, with light support if needed.

outcome_effects: Cannot squat as deep.
Cannot keep the heels down and chest tall.

faults.description: Stance width does not suit your hips: too narrow, too wide, or sumo.

causes.cause: Defaulting to a stance without testing it.
Long femurs with a narrow straight-footed stance.
Limited hip flexion and rotation.

fixes.idea: Find your stance by pulling the knees toward the chest on your back, then adjust and test.
Use a slightly wider stance with some toe-out for long femurs.
Stay just outside hip width and avoid a sumo stance.

outcome_effects: Low back rounding or tipping back.
Instability and falling sideways.
A sumo stance doesn't suit progression to weighted or overhead squats.
faults.disagreement: Source 5 rejects wide sumo stances, while source 6 recommends a wider stance for long femurs; all agree the width should suit the individual.

faults.description: Reaching the arms out in front to stay balanced.

causes.cause: Hips go back without the knees travelling forward, so weight shifts back.
Limited knee and ankle forward movement.

fixes.idea: Hold a weight at the chest (goblet squat) or keep the arms at the chest or overhead.
Stop where you feel the need to counterbalance and work from there.
Use hips back, chest out, then bend the knees.

outcome_effects: Poor balance is reinforced and progress stalls.
Load shifts to the knees, with less glute use.
faults.disagreement: Sources 8 and 10 put the arms out in front as part of normal technique.

faults.description: Tipping backward, with weight too far on the heels or toes.

causes.cause: Pressure too far back on the heels or toes rather than the whole foot.
Not sequencing hips back and chest out before the knees bend.
Long femurs with a narrow stance, or limited hip and ankle mobility.

fixes.idea: Use the tripod foot: big toe, little toe and heel.
Widen the stance with some toe-out and raise the heels.
Do daily bottom-position holds.

outcome_effects: The centre of mass shifts back and you tip over.
Toe pressure stresses the knees.

faults.description: The hips rise or move first and the chest lags, turning the squat into a good morning.

causes.cause: Letting the hips move first at the bottom, breaking the chest-pelvis link.
Fatigue later in a set and poor coordination.
Weak quads relative to glutes and lower back.

fixes.idea: Move chest and pelvis as one unit so they rise at the same rate.
Use pause squats with lighter weight, pausing halfway up.
Drive the chest up out of the bottom.

outcome_effects: Bar drifts forward and the torso leans far forward.
More lumbar and shear stress, and a weaker, less efficient squat.

faults.description: Stopping high at the bottom or not standing fully at the top.

causes.cause: Knees not shoved out.
Cutting the squat short instead of standing all the way up.

fixes.idea: Shove the knees out more and squat to full depth every rep.
Push the hips forward and squeeze the glutes at the top.

outcome_effects: Squats are small and incomplete.

faults.description: Not bracing the core, or breathing out on the way up during heavy sets, causing wobble.

causes.cause: Following the advice to breathe in on the way down and out on the way up.
Letting go of support without bracing.

fixes.idea: Take a big breath into the abdomen, brace and hold it down and up, then exhale at the top.
Brace the core before lowering.

outcome_effects: Instability and a less stable squat.
Less protection for the lower back.
faults.disagreement: Source 3 says to brace on the way down and breathe out as you finish coming up.

faults.description: Foot angle is wrong: toes screw out mid-rep, or point straight ahead when they should turn out.

causes.cause: Assuming a forward-pointing stance by default.
The body takes the path of least resistance when restricted or tight.

fixes.idea: Point the toes out about 30 degrees.
Reset the feet forward each rep and work on mobility.

faults.disagreement: Source 8 treats toes turning out as a compensation and wants them forward. Source 9 says toes straight ahead is the fault and wants about 30 degrees out.

faults.description: The lower back extends into a big arch at the bottom.

causes.cause: Loss of core control.
Hip flexor and quad tension pulling the pelvis into anterior tilt.

fixes.idea: Keep the ribs stacked over the pelvis, as if bracing for a punch.
Do mobility work for the hip flexors and quads.

outcome_effects: Control of the squat is lost.

faults.description: Torso held upright instead of inclined at about 45 degrees.

causes.cause: Not leaning forward or sitting back enough.

fixes.idea: Sit back, lean forward and point the nipples at the floor.

outcome_effects: Balance is lost at the bottom.
faults.disagreement: Source 9 wants a torso inclined about 45 degrees, but sources 3, 6, 8 and 10 want an upright torso and chest.

faults.description: The feet turn out but the knees stay pointing straight ahead.

causes.cause: Rotating only the foot and forgetting the rest of the leg.

fixes.idea: Think about rotating the knees outward instead of the feet.

outcome_effects: Torque at the knee and disrupted tracking.
Patella problems and pain.

faults.description: Forcing depth through passive stretching instead of controlled range.

causes.cause: Relying on stretching rather than strength.

fixes.idea: Hold the bottom with light weight to build active flexibility.

outcome_effects: Heels pop up and the back rounds.
The range is not usable.

faults.description: Sliding to one side at the bottom or on the way up.

causes.cause: Trying to shift onto the stronger leg.
Strength differences between the legs.

fixes.idea: Add unilateral work such as Bulgarian split squats, step-ups or lunges.
Use that work to find and fix imbalances.

outcome_effects: Uneven loading toward the stronger leg, with a risk of hip impingement or labral tear.

faults.description: Holding the knees back so they can't pass the toes.

causes.cause: Having heard that knees shouldn't go past the toes.

fixes.idea: Let the shins track forward over the toes naturally.

outcome_effects: Can't reach proper depth.
faults.disagreement: Source 3 calls knees shooting far past the toes bad for the knees, though it accepts this at low depth. Sources 0, 1, 5 and 7 want the knees to travel forward.

faults.description: Knees shoot forward excessively over the toes, breaking the straight shin line.

fixes.idea: Hinge the hips back and keep the shins in a straight line.

outcome_effects: Stress on the knees.
faults.disagreement: Source 0 says holding the knees back is the fault, and sources 1, 5 and 7 want the knees travelling forward.

faults.description: Starting the squat by bending the knees instead of hinging the hips back.

causes.cause: Believing the squat is mainly a knee-bending movement.

fixes.idea: Practise hinging so the hips go back and down before the knees bend.

faults.description: Hips feel pinchy and tight at the front in the squat.

causes.cause: Limited hip internal rotation.
Poor spine and core stability.

fixes.idea: Do side planks for the outer hip muscles and spine stability.
Practise hip internal rotation on the floor and in a squat.
Do single-leg glute bridges.

outcome_effects: An uncomfortable squat.
faults.disagreement: Source 7 says constant hip stretching is not the answer for most people.
